title: Throughput Alignment & SLA Triage Playbook for Enterprise Dedicated Onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and triage playbook for enterprise dedicated capacity requests that maps customer workload profiles to SLA targets, reserved throughput (RTUs), preferred GPU class, and an autoscaling policy recommendation. This ticket codifies scoring rules, example scenarios, decision templates for Sales/CS, and an operational runbook for handoff to Capacity Operations.
background: We frequently see enterprise requests that mix latency-sensitive and throughput-heavy batch workloads. Sales/CS need a fast deterministic decision path to propose commitment sizes and SLAs without over-provisioning or leaving customers under-served. Current ad-hoc sizing creates rework during onboarding and inconsistent promises to customers.
goal: Ship a standardized triage rubric + intake questionnaire + GPU mapping table + scaling policy matrix that reduces sizing turnaround time to <48 hours for canonical requests and produces a recommended contract template (RTUs, GPU class, SLAs, burst rules).
acceptance_criteria: Public intake form template for Sales/CS (Confluence) with required fields and sample answers
Triage rubric with numeric scoring (0-100) covering latency SLA, QPS, sequence length distribution, KV-cache friendliness, burst profile
GPU class mapping table (A100/RTX6000/H100 equivalents) expressed as rules and fallback ladder
Scaling policy matrix: target SLOs, autoscaling thresholds, burst credit rules, preemption policies
Handoff checklist for Capacity Ops including PR checklist and estimations; runbook link added
Pilot applied to two incoming enterprise requests and comparison logged in onboarding dashboard
triage_rubric: Score components: latency_sensitivity (0-30), steady_qps (0-30), burst_factor (0-15), sequence_complexity (0-15), data_sensitivity (0-10). Total >=75 -> dedicated-high SLA lane (P95 <150ms, 99th <300ms); 50-74 -> dedicated-standard lane (P95 <300ms); <50 -> shared or burstable reserved pool.
intake_form_fields: Primary use case and user flows (chat vs batch vs embedding)
Model family / architecture and quantization tolerance
Estimated daily token volume and growth forecast
recommended_gpu_map: Heuristic mapping: RTUs <2k tokens/sec and P95>500ms -> GPU-tier C (eg. RTX6000 family); 2k-10k tokens/sec or P95 200-500ms -> GPU-tier B (eg. A100-40GB equiv); >10k tokens/sec or P95 <200ms -> GPU-tier A (eg. H100-80GB equiv). Apply sequence-length multiplier: if average sequence >1024 tokens, bump one tier. For KV-cache-heavy workloads, prefer GPU with larger VRAM or multi-GPU KV shard configuration.
scaling_policies: Conservative: reserved headroom=20% of steady RTU, scale threshold=85% sustained for 3m, burst credits available for 30s. Canary ramp for new deployments.
Aggressive: reserved headroom=10%, scale threshold=92% for 60s, allow pre-warmed burst pool (shared) with automatic fallback to lower-cost variant on sustained >5m overload.
Latency-priority: prioritize P95 latency; autoscale on queue latency crossing 50% of SLA, use smaller batch sizes under latency pressure, block batch aggregation when P95 > target.

Cost-priority: schedule non-urgent batch during off-peak windows, allow lower-precision quantized variants for background jobs, set soft-fallback to best-effort shared pool when sustained utilization >120% for >10m.
sample_customer_scenarios: Realtime chat product: target P95 120ms, steady 1.5k req/s, bursts 5x for 30s. Triage -> Tier A H100 pool, RTUs=2.5k, latency-priority policy, burst credits 30s
Embedding generation for search indexing: batch jobs 200k docs overnight, low latency, triage -> Tier B A100 pool, schedule off-peak, cost-priority policy, allow quantized model variant
Financial compliance inference: lower throughput but strict data residency, triage -> dedicated private VPC deploy with Tier B, security_review_required=true, audit logging enabled
risks_and_mitigations: Overcommitation: mitigation - conservative headroom default + explicit note in customer contract about sustained_overage handling
Incorrect model assumptions: mitigation - include model verification step in intake and require sample trace for profiling
Operational complexity on onboarding: mitigation - provide Capacity Ops checklist and one-hour kick-off alignment call
